project_overview.name: Course Translation Hub
project_overview.description: An automated system leveraging AI agents to parse, translate, and repackage IMSCC Canvas course exports.

core_files.imsmanifest.xml: The main manifest file. It maps resource identifiers (used in the hash directories) to their corresponding files and outlines the course structure (modules, item sequences). Treat this as the definitive index.
core_files.app/link_mapping.json: A multi-language JSON mapping of English web links to their localized counterparts (PTBR, SPA, etc.). Used by the LinkProcessor (in app/core/) to automatically replace links before bot translation. Lives inside the app/ directory alongside the controller.

directories.course_settings/: Contains global configuration files for the course, including the main syllabus page (e.g., syllabus.html) and course_settings.xml (which provides the course code).
directories.wiki_content/: Contains Canvas Pages stored as standard HTML files. These are primary targets for textual translation.
directories.web_resources/: Contains static files, images, or documents linked within the course pages.
directories.non_cc_assessments/: Contains quizzes and assessments that might not follow the standard Common Cartridge specification.
directories.hash_directories/: Folders named with unique alphanumeric hashes (e.g., 'g038b...'). These contain metadata for assignments, discussions, quizzes, and rubrics (e.g., assessment_meta.xml, assessment_qti.xml, assignment_settings.xml). Look inside these XML files for description tags and text that require translation.
directories.app/: Contains the main application code: controller.py, main_ui.py, course_auditor.py, reprocess_failed.py, and the architecture instructions JSON.
directories.app/bots/: Contains the specialized translation and auditing bots (html_bot.py, xml_bot.py, txt_bot.py, image_bot.py, auditor_bot.py, scripturecheck_bot.py, qa_audit_bot.py, api_utils.py, edtech_bot.py), plus the shared translation_log.txt.
directories.app/core/: Contains the modularized architecture components: LinkProcessor (link_processor.py), WorkspaceManager (workspace_manager.py), and DashboardGenerator (dashboard_generator.py), decoupled from the main controller.
directories.app/scripts/: Contains standalone automation scripts, such as migrate_groups.py which interacts with the Canvas API to extract, translate, and push student groups to a new course shell.
directories.Glossary/: Contains a unified 'glossary.json' for terms standardization and a 'scriptures/' subfolder containing language-specific subfolders: por/ (Portuguese), spa/ (Spanish), eng/ (English source references), and fra/ (French — reserved for future use). The por/ and spa/ folders contain modern scriptures JSON files used by ScriptureCheckBot to crosscheck references.
directories.Courses to Translate/: Contains the temporary course files, including the raw .imscc Canvas exports and their respective unzipped working directories. Finalized translations (e.g., _PTBR output folders) and repackaged .imscc files are also saved here.
directories.Courses to Audit/: Contains the .imscc Canvas exports (English Canon and Translated versions) to be unzipped and compared by the course auditor process.
directories.Reports/: Contains all generated output reports. Both the translation dashboard Excel ('{CourseName} Translation Report.xlsx') and the audit report Excel ('Audit_Report_{CourseName}.xlsx') are saved here.

bot_instructions.workspace_management: All controllers and scripts must strictly look for and operate on unzipped course exports and raw .imscc files exclusively within the 'Courses to Translate/' directory. Finalized translations (e.g., _PTBR output folders) and repackaged .imscc files must also be saved directly into the 'Courses to Translate/' directory. The root hub directory must remain clean of course files.
bot_instructions.temporary_override: CRITICAL: The user currently only has the Gemini API key. All agents (including HTML, XML, QTI, Document, and Image bots) MUST temporarily use Gemini instead of Claude or ChatGPT.
bot_instructions.mandatory_pre_check: All agent bots MUST read this file (Course_Translation_Hub_ArchitectureAndInstructions.json) before beginning any translation tasks.
logging_requirements: All bots (including the controller and specialized bots) MUST implement an internal logging mechanism.
All bots and the controller must append their logs to a single shared text-based log file (translation_log.txt) in the app/bots/ directory. Individual log files are not used.
Every significant action, such as file delegation, successful translation, skipped files, errors, and warnings, must be recorded in the shared log file as well as printed to standard output.
The controller bot must extract the Course Name and Course Code from the imsmanifest.xml or course_settings.xml and log it as '[System] CourseInfo: {course_name}|{course_code}'.

The controller bot must log link mapping actions (e.g., GoogleLinkStripped, SkippedLink, SkippedLinkWithComment, CommentedLink) to track link modifications, using the human-readable page title for context.

Upon successful translation of a file, the controller must extract the page's title using BeautifulSoup (falling back to the filename) and log it as '[System] TranslatedPage: {page_title} | {filepath}'.

The text logs are parsed and visualized by the DashboardGenerator (app/core/dashboard_generator.py) into '{CourseName} Translation Report.xlsx' saved in the Reports/ directory. The dashboard includes a 'Dashboard' tab showing the Course Name & Code, KPI metrics, skipped files list, and file type counts; a 'Bot Analysis' tab with per-bot statistics and a stacked chart; a 'Raw Logs' tab with all parsed log entries; a 'Translated Pages' tab listing deduplicated translated page titles (flagging any duplicate names with 'Duplicate Name (FIX EN Course)'); and a 'Link Actions' tab.

The 'Link Actions' tab consolidates Google Links (which get stripped of tracking parameters and flagged with 'FIX EN Course'), Skipped Links (logged as Info without warnings), and Commented Links (where users provided notes during link mapping).

api_assignments.ChatGPT: Use for OCR of images containing embedded text. (Note: Standalone image replacement agents are currently unimplemented).
api_assignments.Claude: Use for HTMLTranslationAgent, XMLTranslationAgent, QTITranslationAgent, and DocumentTranslationAgent (docx, pptx). Crucial for strict adherence to complex formatting constraints, preserving brackets, and ensuring zero tag modification. (Note: Document agents are currently unapproved/unimplemented).
api_assignments.Gemini: All current bots (controller, HTML, XML, text, auditor, scripturecheck, qa_audit, image) use gemini-3.5-flash for translation and processing.

api_resilience.rate_limits: All bots MUST implement an exponential backoff retry mechanism (via app/bots/api_utils.py call_gemini_with_retry) to gracefully handle 429 Rate Limit errors, internal server errors (500/503), 504 Gateway Timeouts, and deadline exceeded errors, given the concurrency of translations.
api_resilience.invalid_keys: All bots MUST validate their API keys on initialization (checking key presence via the client_ready flag) and the shared api_utils catches 400 Bad Request/InvalidArgument exceptions to prevent empty file overwrites or silent failures.

multi_agent_strategy.controller_bot: The primary bot (controller.py) acts as the background translator engine, but the overall workflow is orchestrated by main_ui.py. Phase 1: Pre-flight checks in UI. The UI silently extracts the source_course_id via WorkspaceManager and checks if the Canvas course has groups. If groups exist, the UI prompts for the EN Master Link (validating against the source ID) and the PT Master URL. Phase 2: Sequential link pre-processing (delegated to LinkProcessor in app/core/link_processor.py) which checks against app/link_mapping.json. Phase 3: Concurrent file delegation (via ThreadPoolExecutor with max_workers=3) to specialized subagents for translation. Phase 4: Conditional Group Migration. If groups exist, main_ui.py pauses with a popup instructing the user to import the .imscc package into Canvas. Upon clicking OK, it delegates to app/scripts/migrate_groups.py to fetch, translate, and push groups to the Target Course shell. Phase 5: An interactive post-translation checklist is presented via the UI (main_ui.py) reminding the user of manual Canvas configuration steps.
multi_agent_strategy.specialized_bots: For each file or specific file type (e.g., HTML, XML), the controller bot MUST invoke a specialized subagent/bot to perform the actual parsing and translation.
multi_agent_strategy.scripturecheck_bot: A local pre-processing utility (scripturecheck_bot.py) that uses Regular Expressions to extract scripture references from the source text and fetches their official translations from the 'Glossary/scriptures/{lang}/' folder (where lang is 'por' for PTBR or 'spa' for SPA) to be injected into the translation prompt as constraints. TODO: Extend to support Bible references.
multi_agent_strategy.glossary_audit_bot: A local pre-processing utility (auditor_bot.py, class GlossaryAuditBot) that scans the source text for English glossary terms from Glossary/glossary.json and passes only the relevant glossary terms (filtered by target language) as constraints to the translation prompt.
multi_agent_strategy.qa_audit_bot: A specialized subagent (qa_audit_bot.py, class QAAuditBot) used by course_auditor.py. Has two capabilities: (1) audit_content() which compares the English (Canon) Canvas page against its translated counterpart, identifying Missing, Extra, Different Content, and Different Order discrepancies; (2) pair_unmatched_files() which uses AI to match unmatched English files to their translated counterparts when filenames have changed (e.g., W03 → S03 renaming scenarios).

agent_mapping.html: HTMLTranslationAgent (html_bot.py) - Responsible for parsing HTML DOM using BeautifulSoup to dynamically map and protect sensitive attributes (like src and href URLs) with UUID placeholders before translating textual content. It also delegates tags to ImageProcessorBot. ImageProcessorBot translates existing alt texts, or if missing, fetches the image to generate an English description first (which is logged to the dashboard), and then translates it into the target language.
agent_mapping.xml: XMLTranslationAgent (xml_bot.py) - Responsible for safely translating localized text strings inside XML tags using BeautifulSoup. Extracts only the inner text of specific nodes (such as title, mattext, description, long_description, fieldentry, and text) and translates them via a custom XML-like delimiter. It also delegates tags within inner HTML to ImageProcessorBot for the same 2-step EN-to-Target alt text generation.
agent_mapping.qti: QTITranslationAgent - Maps to XMLTranslationBot, sharing the same class as XML. Responsible for specialized Canvas QTI assessment files (quizzes), ensuring assessment structures remain valid.
agent_mapping.txt: TextTranslationAgent (txt_bot.py) - Responsible for plain text file translation.
agent_mapping.docx: DocumentTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED/PENDING APPROVAL] Responsible for extracting, translating, and repacking Microsoft Word documents.
agent_mapping.pptx: DocumentTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED/PENDING APPROVAL] Responsible for extracting, translating, and repacking Microsoft PowerPoint presentations.
agent_mapping.jpg: ImageTranslationAgent - [UNIMPLEMENTED] For localized versions of images. Note: Alt text is handled inline by ImageProcessorBot.
agent_mapping.DS_Store: IGNORE - System files should be skipped by the controller.
agent_mapping.UNKNOWN: CRITICAL: Any unmapped file extension should trigger the unknown_architecture_protocol.

translation_guidelines: The target language for all translations will be either Portuguese (Brazil) or Spanish, as directed by the user.
Only translate textual content intended for students.

For the setup notes page (files containing 'setup-notes'), the controller must translate ONLY the cells of the tables. The English text must not be replaced, but instead the translation must be appended with a slash (e.g., 'Modules / Módulos'). The rest of the page remains in English.

For files related to the Teaching Notes and Student Outreach page (e.g., containing 'teaching-notes-and-student-outreach'), the controller must automatically apply a hardcoded glossary of Canvas navigation terms to ensure instructor-facing terminology matches expected standards. NOTE: The current hardcoded glossary is Portuguese-only and must be extended for Spanish when SPA translation of Teaching Notes pages is needed.

For files related to the Teaching Notes and Student Outreach page, the bots must empty the contents of the 'Release Notes' section (leaving only the translated 'Release Notes' header), as translated courses start with a fresh version history.
For XML question banks and quizzes, the word 'Question' in the title attribute of <item> nodes must be translated to the target language.
Preserve all HTML structure, Canvas-specific classes, div wrappers, and inline styles exactly as they are.

Preserve all XML tags, attributes, and file names. Do not translate metadata keys, IDs, or manifest identifiers (except for the 'title' attribute on <item> nodes where 'Question' is translated, and the <fieldentry> content for 'bank_title' labels).
Ensure translated HTML or XML does not break parsing rules.

Whenever the controller finds a churchofjesuschrist.org link, it must change the link parameter to the target language (e.g., lang=por for Portuguese or lang=spa for Spanish). If no lang parameter exists, one is appended.

If the controller finds the obsolete Google Forms link (ID: 1FAIpQLSe2Tc7N-ltFhqmqSNXtftVF7wMpyPw5bHPCtuYwnAm4PN7UEA), it must log it as an ObsoleteLink and mark it in the final report to tell the user to remove it from the EN course and make changes in Canvas.

The controller must programmatically replace the standalone word 'Missing' (or 'missing') in XML files (like rubrics) with 'Não Entregue' (for PTBR) or 'No Entregado' (for SPA) prior to passing the content to the XML bot, to ensure accurate rubric rendering.
The XML bot must explicitly skip translating the exact strings 'True' and 'False' inside <mattext> tags to prevent Canvas from demoting true_false_question types to Multiple Choice during import.
bot_instructions.unknown_architecture_protocol: If the controller encounters a file type that is not mapped to an active bot, it must gracefully skip the file and log a warning ('Skipping unsupported file architecture for extension...'). It should not halt execution.
bot_instructions.user_intervention_required: User intervention is not required for unknown file types; the controller will simply skip them and proceed with the rest of the translation batch.

agent_prompts.HTMLTranslationAgent_PTBR: Role & Objective You are an expert academic translator specializing in Portuguese. Your singular objective is to translate text within HTML tags into standard, grammatically correct Portuguese that is universally understood across all Portuguese-speaking regions (including Europe, Africa, and Brazil), appropriate for undergraduate students. In the rare event of an irreconcilable regional conflict, fall back to Brazilian Portuguese conventions. Input Context You will receive fragmented HTML chunks. The code will often be incomplete or have unmatched/open tags. Strict Constraints Localization & Transcreation: DO NOT translate word-by-word. Your goal is to LOCALIZE the content. Restructure sentences, use natural idiomatic phrasing, and adapt expressions so they read fluidly and professionally to a native speaker. Preserve the original intent, tone, and academic rigor, but prioritize natural flow over literal translation. Output Format: You MUST wrap your entire final output inside an HTML markdown code block (```html at the beginning and ``` at the end). Never output raw HTML outside of these backticks. Zero Interaction: Do NOT output any conversational filler, greetings, acknowledgments, or explanations. Only output the code block. Zero Tag Modification: Do NOT translate, modify, add, or remove ANY HTML tags. Do NOT attempt to "fix" or auto-close open tags. Output the exact original tag structure. Translate ONLY inner text values. Formatting Integrity: Maintain exact original indentation, line breaks, and spacing of the HTML structure. INLINE TAG SPACING: You MUST meticulously preserve spaces before and after inline HTML tags (like , , , , , ). For example, translate 'The mean is' as 'A média é' (with spaces), NOT 'Amédiaé'. Failure to preserve spacing around inline tags will cause words to merge together and is unacceptable. Language & Gender Neutrality: Use grammatically correct, gender-neutral terminology naturally available in the language (e.g., prefer estudante over aluno(a) or pessoa over homem/mulher). Strict Restriction: You must completely avoid artificial gender-neutral word endings (such as substituting "o" or "a" with "e") and neologisms (such as todes). STRICT WHITESPACE NORMALIZATION: You must NEVER output the invisible Alt+0160 character (non-breaking space / U+00A0), and you must NEVER output the HTML entity  . You must actively replace any non-breaking spaces or   entities from the original text with standard normal spaces (U+0020) in your final output. Institutional Guidelines Deity & Reverence: Capitalize all names, titles, and pronouns referring to Deity (e.g., Ele, Dele). However, lowercase pronouns referring to heavenly parents. Scriptural Formats: Do not italicize the titles of the standard works or their specific parts (e.g., Bíblia, O Livro de Mórmon). Church Nomenclature: Always use the full official name of the Church as defined in the glossary. Do not use terms like "Mormon Church", "LDS Church", or "Mormonism". Quotation Integrity: Maintain the exact formatting, spelling, and punctuation of quoted material. If an interpolation, translation of a term, or grammatical correction is necessary within a quote, you must enclose the added text in brackets [ ]. \n\nRelease Notes: When translating Teaching Notes or Student Outreach pages, empty out all content under the 'Release Notes' section (e.g. leaving only the translated or heading), as translated courses start with a fresh version history.

agent_prompts.XMLTranslationAgent_PTBR:
Role & Objective

You are an expert academic translator specializing in Portuguese. Your singular objective is to translate human-readable text content inside XML <translate_item> tags into standard, grammatically correct Portuguese that is universally understood across all Portuguese-speaking regions (including Europe, Africa, and Brazil), appropriate for undergraduate students. In the rare event of an irreconcilable regional conflict, fall back to Brazilian Portuguese conventions.

Input Context

You will receive a set of XML-like <translate_item> tags, each with an 'id' attribute. Each tag contains text that may include embedded HTML tags (like <strong>, <b>, <em>, <a>).

Strict Constraints

Localization & Transcreation: DO NOT translate word-by-word. Your goal is to LOCALIZE the content. Restructure sentences, use natural idiomatic phrasing, and adapt expressions so they read fluidly and professionally to a native speaker. Preserve the original intent, tone, and academic rigor, but prioritize natural flow over literal translation.

Output Format: Return exactly the same <translate_item> XML-like structure with the translated text. Keep the 'id' attributes intact and unmodified. Do NOT output any markdown code blocks or extra formatting.

Zero Interaction: Do NOT output any conversational filler, greetings, acknowledgments, or explanations. Only output the translated <translate_item> tags.

Preserve Inline HTML: If the content contains inline HTML tags (such as <strong>, <b>, <em>, <a href=...>), maintain them exactly as they are. Translate ONLY the text within and around these tags.

Do NOT Translate: URLs, filenames, the 'id' attribute values, or any metadata identifiers.

Language & Gender Neutrality: Use grammatically correct, gender-neutral terminology naturally available in the language (e.g., prefer estudante over aluno(a) or pessoa over homem/mulher). Strict Restriction: You must completely avoid artificial gender-neutral word endings (such as substituting "o" or "a" with "e") and neologisms (such as todes).

STRICT WHITESPACE NORMALIZATION: You must NEVER output the invisible Alt+0160 character (non-breaking space / U+00A0), and you must NEVER output the HTML entity  . You must actively replace any non-breaking spaces or   entities from the original text with standard normal spaces (U+0020) in your final output.

Institutional Guidelines

Deity & Reverence: Capitalize all names, titles, and pronouns referring to Deity (e.g., Ele, Dele). However, lowercase pronouns referring to heavenly parents.

Scriptural Formats: Do not italicize the titles of the standard works or their specific parts (e.g., Bíblia, O Livro de Mórmon).

Church Nomenclature: Always use the full official name of the Church as defined in the glossary. Do not use terms like "Mormon Church", "LDS Church", or "Mormonism".

Quotation Integrity: Maintain the exact formatting, spelling, and punctuation of quoted material. If an interpolation, translation of a term, or grammatical correction is necessary within a quote, you must enclose the added text in brackets [ ].

Role & Objective

You are an expert academic translator specializing in Portuguese. Scriptural Formats: Do not italicize the titles of the standard works (e.g., Bíblia, O Livro de Mórmon).

workflow: The UI prompts the user to select the English (Original) and Translated IMSCC files.
The system internally copies the selected .imscc files to the 'Courses to Audit/' directory.
The CourseAuditor extracts both Canvas packages into temporary 'temp_en' and 'temp_pt' folders inside 'Courses to Audit/'.
It reads the 'imsmanifest.xml' from both packages to securely map the unique Canvas 'identifier' for each file to its relative path.

It cross-references all translatable files (.html and .xml) globally across the entire course to determine matching pairs using a multi-step strategy: (1) Match by Manifest Resource ID, (2) Fallback to Relative Path matching, (3) AI-based pairing via QAAuditBot.pair_unmatched_files() for handling renamed files (e.g., W03 → S03), (4) Flag remaining unmatched EN files as 'Missing in Translated', and (5) Flag remaining unmatched PT files as 'Extra in Translated'.
The auditor iterates through every matched file pair.
For HTML pages, it performs a strict link audit to verify all external web URLs (http/https) match exactly between English and Translated pages, flagging any missing or extra links.

For files containing sufficient text (length > 10), it leverages gemini-3.5-flash via the QAAuditBot to perform an advanced LLM-based quality assurance check, categorizing discrepancies as Missing, Extra, Different Content, or Different Order.

The results are safely parsed and exported directly into a 3-tab Excel report ('Audit_Report_{CourseName}.xlsx') saved in the Reports/ directory: 'Page Audit Report' (file level match status with EN/PT page names), 'Content Audit Report' (text/layout/meaning discrepancies from LLM analysis), and 'Links Audit Reports' (URL discrepancies for HTML pages).

utility_scripts.reprocess_failed.py: A utility script that parses the translation_log.txt to find files that failed on the 3rd XML parse attempt, re-initializes the TranslationController, and reprocesses only those failed files. Uses controller.workspace.compress_to_imscc(controller._log) for repackaging.

workflow: The UI prompts the user for the EdTech Book URL and target language.

Extraction Phase: The EdTechScraperBot launches a Chromium browser via Playwright (using a persistent profile 'playwright_profile' for login sessions). It navigates the book index, clicks the ToggleEditor button for each chapter, and extracts the raw HTML from the code-box.

Title Piggybacking: During extraction, the chapter title is scraped and prepended to the raw HTML wrapped in a hidden <div id="edtech-meta-title"> to force the LLM to translate it along with the chapter body.

Translation Phase: The extracted raw HTML files are saved to 'edtech_workspace/raw_html/'. The standard TranslationController is invoked to process the directory. It automatically translates the files into 'edtech_workspace/raw_html_PTBR/' (or corresponding language).

Injection Phase: The EdTechScraperBot iterates over the original URLs again. For each page, it extracts the translated title from the piggybacked div, strips it from the HTML, injects the translated HTML back into the code-box, repopulates the title field, and automates clicking 'Apply' and 'Save'.

# Claude Integration — Comprehensive Content Analysis Bots

## Background

The Translation Hub currently uses **Gemini 3.5 Flash** for all translation and auditing tasks. The user wants to introduce **Claude (Anthropic)** as a dedicated analytical engine for two new use cases that go beyond file-by-file comparison:

1. **Intra-Course Consistency Analysis** — Analyze the *entire* translated course package holistically to detect inconsistencies in terminology, tone, formatting conventions, glossary adherence, and instructional flow across all pages.
2. **Course vs EdTech Cross-Reference Analysis** — Compare the translated Canvas course package against the translated EdTech book content to ensure alignment, cohesion, and consistency between the two deliverables.

These are fundamentally different from the existing `QAAuditBot` (which does page-by-page EN↔PT comparison). Claude will instead act as a **holistic reviewer** that ingests the full scope of content.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The `anthropic` package is already in `requirements.txt`, but no Claude API key exists in `.env` yet. You'll need to add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<your_key>` to `.env` before using the new bots.

---

## Proposed Changes

### Configuration & API Layer

#### [MODIFY] [.env](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/.env)
Add the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` variable:
```diff
 GEMINI_API_KEY=...
 CANVAS_API_URL=...
 CANVAS_API_TOKEN=...
+ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<your_claude_api_key>
```

#### [NEW] [claude_api_utils.py](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/bots/claude_api_utils.py)
A new API utility module for Anthropic, mirroring the existing `api_utils.py` pattern but for the Claude Messages API:
- `call_claude_with_retry(client, model, system, messages, max_retries, initial_delay, log_func)` — exponential backoff for `429`, `500`, `529` (overloaded), and timeout errors.
- Validates API key presence on import (raises early).
- Uses the `anthropic.Anthropic()` client pattern (not the legacy completions API).
- Default model: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514` (best balance of intelligence and cost for analysis tasks; can be switched to Opus for maximum quality if budget allows).

> [!NOTE]
> **Model choice rationale**: Claude Sonnet 4 is recommended as the default for these analysis bots because the workload is heavy on reasoning over large text corpora. Opus would provide the highest quality but at ~5× the cost. The model name will be configurable via the bot constructor so you can upgrade per task.

---

### New Bot: Course Consistency Analyzer

#### [NEW] [consistency_bot.py](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/bots/consistency_bot.py)
A new `CourseConsistencyBot` class that analyzes an entire translated course package for internal consistency.

**Constructor**: `CourseConsistencyBot(api_key=None, model_name="claude-sonnet-4-20250514")`
- Initializes the Anthropic client.
- Loads glossary from `Glossary/glossary.json` for cross-checking.

**Core method**: `analyze_course(course_dir, target_language) → list[dict]`
- Walks the translated course directory and collects all `.html` and `.xml` content.
- Batches pages into logical groups (by module/week structure parsed from `imsmanifest.xml`).
- Sends batched content to Claude with a system prompt that instructs it to look for:
  - **Terminology drift**: Same English concept translated differently across pages (e.g., "assignment" → "tarefa" in one page but "atividade" in another).
  - **Glossary violations**: Terms that deviate from `glossary.json` definitions.
  - **Tone inconsistency**: Shifts between formal/informal register across pages.
  - **Formatting pattern breaks**: Inconsistent use of bold/italic, heading levels, or list styles.
  - **Scripture reference inconsistencies**: Different formatting or translations of the same scripture across pages.
  - **Navigation/link label mismatches**: Module names or cross-references that don't match.
- Returns structured results as a list of dicts: `{page, issue_type, detail, severity, suggestion}`.

**Chunking strategy**: Claude's context window (200K tokens) is large enough to analyze a full course in 2–4 batches. The bot will:
1. Extract text content from all pages (stripping HTML structure to reduce token count).
2. Group pages by module (using manifest data).
3. Send each module group + the glossary as a single request.
4. Send a final "cross-module" summary request that references the per-module findings.

---

### New Bot: Course vs EdTech Cross-Analyzer

#### [NEW] [cross_analysis_bot.py](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/bots/cross_analysis_bot.py)
A new `CrossAnalysisBot` class that compares translated Canvas content against translated EdTech book content.

**Constructor**: `CrossAnalysisBot(api_key=None, model_name="claude-sonnet-4-20250514")`

**Core method**: `analyze_alignment(course_dir, edtech_dir, target_language) → list[dict]`
- Reads translated course pages from the IMSCC output directory.
- Reads translated EdTech HTML files from `edtech_workspace/raw_html_{LANG}/`.
- Sends paired/grouped content to Claude with a system prompt focused on:
  - **Content alignment**: Topics covered in the course that reference or should reference EdTech content, and vice versa.
  - **Terminology consistency**: Same concepts using the same translated terms in both the course and the book.
  - **Cross-reference integrity**: Links or mentions in course pages that point to EdTech chapters — verifying the referenced content actually matches.
  - **Pedagogical cohesion**: Ensuring the instructional narrative flows logically between the course and the supplementary book material.
  - **Missing coverage**: Content in the EdTech book not referenced by the course, or course topics that lack supporting book material.
- Returns: `{course_page, edtech_chapter, issue_type, detail, severity, suggestion}`.

---

### New Orchestrator: Claude Analysis Runner

#### [NEW] [claude_analyzer.py](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/claude_analyzer.py)
An orchestrator module (similar to `course_auditor.py`) that coordinates the two new bots:

- `ClaudeAnalyzer(course_imscc_or_dir, edtech_dir=None, target_language="PTBR")`
- `run_consistency_analysis()` — Extracts the course, runs `CourseConsistencyBot`, exports results.
- `run_cross_analysis()` — Validates both directories exist, runs `CrossAnalysisBot`, exports results.
- `run_full_analysis()` — Runs both sequentially.
- Exports results to `Reports/Claude_Analysis_{CourseName}.xlsx` with tabs:
  - **Consistency Report** — Intra-course issues.
  - **Cross-Reference Report** — Course vs EdTech issues (if EdTech dir provided).
  - **Summary** — High-level dashboard with issue counts by severity and type.

---

### UI Integration

#### [MODIFY] [main_ui.py](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/main_ui.py)
Add a new **"Claude Analysis"** section to the UI (a new `LabelFrame` between the Audit section and the Progress bar):

- **Radio buttons**: "Course Consistency Only" / "Course + EdTech Cross-Analysis" / "Full Analysis"
- **Button**: "Run Claude Analysis"
- **Workflow**:
  1. Prompts user to select the translated IMSCC file.
  2. If cross-analysis mode is selected, also prompts for the EdTech workspace path (or auto-detects from `edtech_workspace/`).
  3. Checks for `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in `.env` — shows an error dialog if missing.
  4. Runs the selected analysis in a background thread, streaming output to the console.
  5. Opens the report file on completion.

---

### Architecture Doc Update

#### [MODIFY] [Course_Translation_Hub_ArchitectureAndInstructions.json](file:///c:/Users/vscaran/Desktop/DevProjects/WWOTranslationHUB/app/Course_Translation_Hub_ArchitectureAndInstructions.json)
- Add Claude to the `api_assignments` section with its designated role (comprehensive analysis).
- Update the `temporary_override` note to reflect that Claude is now used for analysis bots (not translation).
- Add the new bots (`consistency_bot.py`, `cross_analysis_bot.py`) to the `app/bots/` directory description.
- Add `claude_analyzer.py` to the `app/` directory description.
- Document the new analysis process in a new top-level `claude_analysis_process` section.

---

## Open Questions

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Claude model tier**: Should we default to **Sonnet 4** (balanced cost/quality, ~$3/$15 per MTok) or **Opus** (maximum quality, ~$15/$75 per MTok)? Sonnet 4 is likely sufficient for consistency analysis, but Opus would catch more subtle issues. We could also make this user-selectable in the UI.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Analysis scope for Cross-Reference**: When comparing Course vs EdTech, should Claude try to auto-match course pages to EdTech chapters (similar to how `QAAuditBot.pair_unmatched_files` works), or should the user provide an explicit mapping? Auto-matching would be more convenient but less predictable.

> [!NOTE]
> **Existing `temporary_override`**: The architecture doc says "All agents MUST temporarily use Gemini." Since these new Claude bots are *analysis-only* (not translation), they should be exempt from this override. Please confirm this is acceptable.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Unit test for `claude_api_utils.py` retry logic (mock API errors).
- Unit test for `CourseConsistencyBot` text extraction and chunking logic (using a sample course directory).
- Integration test: Run `ClaudeAnalyzer.run_consistency_analysis()` on a small test course and verify the Excel report is generated with the correct tabs and column structure.

### Manual Verification
- Run "Course Consistency Only" analysis on an already-translated PTBR course from `Courses to Translate/` and review the report for meaningful findings.
- Run "Course + EdTech Cross-Analysis" using the existing `edtech_workspace/raw_html_PTBR/` data and verify the cross-reference report.
- Verify the UI button states (disabled during analysis, re-enabled after), console output streaming, and error handling for missing API key.

# Goal Description

The objective is to implement a new feature in the WWOTranslationHUB for translating GitHub-hosted textbooks in Software Development. This pipeline will pull markdown-based textbooks from GitHub, safely translate the human-readable text (ignoring code blocks and markdown syntax), and output a translated repository that can be published or submitted as a Pull Request.

> [!WARNING]
> **Static Site Generators**:
> Are these GitHub textbooks pure Markdown (`.md` / `.mdx`) files, or are they part of a framework (like Docusaurus, MkDocs, or Hugo)? If they are part of a framework, we may also need to translate specific navigation configurations (like `sidebar.json` or `mkdocs.yml`).

## Open Questions

- Should we translate the **Alt Text** of images found inside the Markdown files, similarly to how the HTML bot handles them?
- Are there specific glossary terms for "Software Development" that we should enforce during this translation? (e.g., standardizing translations for terms like "Pull Request", "Commit", "Deployment", "Framework").

---

## Proposed Changes

We will introduce a new pipeline parallel to the Canvas (IMSCC) and EdTech workflows.

### 1. User Interface Integration

#### [MODIFY] `app/main_ui.py`
- Modify the **"Canvas IMSCC file Translation"** section.
- Add two new checkboxes:
  - `[ ] Includes EdTech Book`
  - `[ ] Includes GitHub Textbook`
- **Workflow Update**: When the user clicks "Select Course & Translate" and selects an IMSCC package:
  - If **Includes GitHub Textbook** is checked, prompt the user for the **GitHub Repository URL**.
  - Pass this configuration to the translation thread so the GitHub extraction runs alongside the course translation.

### 2. Workspace & Repository Management

#### [NEW] `app/core/github_manager.py` (or extending WorkspaceManager)
- Responsible for cloning the target GitHub repository into a new local directory: `github_workspace/raw_repo/`.
- **Target Extraction**: Navigate specifically into the `DOCS` directory of the cloned repository and collect all Markdown files to be translated.
- **Output Structure**: Based on the provided GitHub repository URL (e.g., `https://github.com/byui-cse/cse111-course`), the system will automatically derive the target repository name by appending the language suffix (e.g., `-PT` for Portuguese). 
- After translation, it will recreate the structure in `github_workspace/[Original-Repo-Name]-[LANG-SUFFIX]/` (e.g., `cse111-course-PT`).
- The final translated output will be prepared and saved in this new local directory so the user can easily copy or push/pull it into their target repository manually.

### 3. Markdown Translation Bot

#### [NEW] `app/bots/md_bot.py`
- Create a `MarkdownTranslationBot` that specializes in parsing `.md` and `.mdx` files.
- **Parsing Strategy**: It will use Regex or a Markdown parser to separate code blocks (```` ``` ````), inline code (`code`), URLs, and YAML frontmatter from the actual human-readable paragraphs.
- **Prompting**: The system prompt will strictly instruct the AI to preserve all markdown formatting (hashes for headers, asterisks for bold/italics, list hyphens) and *only* translate the text content. 
- It will leverage the existing API utils (using Gemini, or Claude once integrated in Front #1).

### 4. Controller Updates

#### [MODIFY] `app/controller.py`
- Update the `process_file` logic and bot mapping to recognize `.md` and `.mdx` file extensions.
- Route these files to the new `MarkdownTranslationBot`.
- Extend the `_is_already_translated` heuristic to safely check markdown files without counting code blocks as English words.

#### [MODIFY] `Course_Translation_Hub_ArchitectureAndInstructions.json`
- Document the new architecture under a `"github_integration"` block so future agents understand the flow.

### 5. Glossary & Prompts

#### [MODIFY] `Glossary/glossary.json` (or specific software dev glossary)
- Inject a specialized glossary for Software Development terms to prevent the LLM from translating technical terms that should remain in English (e.g., "API", "IDE", "Hash", "String").

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
- Run translation on a sample `.md` file containing complex markdown (tables, code blocks, nested lists, frontmatter) to ensure formatting is perfectly preserved and code blocks are not translated.

- Clone a sample public Github Textbook repository locally.
- Run the hub's new Github pipeline and inspect the output directory.
